title: On the critical contributions of end‐of‐sequence switching to our understanding of sequence variation
abstract: Abstract There remains disagreement regarding whether variability is an operant response dimension. A critical issue related to this disagreement is the extent to which the variation observed under a variability‐reinforcement contingency is directly reinforced versus induced through other factors. The goal of the present research was to improve our understanding of behavioral variability by clarifying the effects of a significant source of between‐sequence variation—namely, end‐of‐sequence switching. Pigeons emitted four‐peck sequences across left and right keys in two experiments. In Experiment 1, sequence variation was significantly greater under a Lag 2 contingency that encouraged switching at the end of sequences relative to contingencies that did not. Experiment 2 extended these findings to an environment that did not require sequence variation. One group earned food only following a sequence with a changeover at its start, and another group only received food following a sequence with a changeover at its end. Only the latter contingency engendered sequence variation. Both experiments confirm that contingencies that promote end‐of‐sequence switching are a critical source of between‐sequence variation. The implications of these findings for the discussion about whether variability is an operant response dimension are presented.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF THE EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS OF BEHAVIOR
